document.heading: AN ORDINANCE ADOPTING SPECIAL STUDY PREZONING FOR THE HESS/LAIRD TERRITORY CONSISTENT WITH THE GENERAL PLAN (AMERICAN CANYON MUNICIPAL CODE CHAPTER 19.50)

citations.citation: City of American Canyon, Cal., Ord. No. 2026-02

recital.text: pursuant to Section 65300 of the State Planning and Zoning Law, the City of American Canyon (City) has adopted a General Plan (the 2040 General Plan Update) to provide comprehensive long-range planning and a blueprint of the City's future form, including land use and circulation maps that specify the roadway network and the distribution of types and intensities of land; and

on May 20, 2025, the City Council of the City of American Canyon adopted Resolution No. 2025-38 adopting the 2040 General Plan Update, including the "Future Study Area" designation of approximately 282 acres located northeast of the City of American Canyon in unincorporated Napa County, California. The property is known as the Hess/Laird Territory (hereafter the "Affected Territory") and identified by Assessor's Parcel Numbers (APNs) 057-090-065 and 057-090-066; and

in March 2026, Hess-Laird property owners initiated proceedings with the Local Area Formation Commission of Napa County ("LAFCO") to annex the Hess-Laird Affected Territory into the City of American Canyon and the American Canyon Fire Protection District, with concurrent and coterminous amendment of the City of American Canyon's Sphere of Influence ("SOI"), which requires an application to the Local Agency Formation Commission of Napa County ("Napa LAFCo") for approval of the proposed reorganization (collectively, "Reorganization Activities"); and
pursuant to Section 56375(a)(7) of the Government Code the City must pre-zone the Affected Territory as a condition to LAFCO's approval of the proposed annexation; and

the City is lead agency and LAFCO is the responsible agency for the Reorganization Activities on the Affected Territory under California Environmental Quality Act ("CEQA"), Public Resources Code section 2000 et seq.; and
notwithstanding any annexation, under Government Code section 65860, the City is obligated to bring zoning into conformance with the Update General Plan; and

the City seeks to pre-zone the Affected Territory as a "special study zone" ("SSZ") within the Special Study Zone District as described in American Canyon Municipal Code Chapter 19.50, consistent with the 2040 General Plan Update and Government Code Section 65859; and

the purpose of the SSZ district is to: (a) allow properties to be zoned or Pre-Zoned until the City has completed appropriate planning studies to determine the types and intensities of land uses through an amendment of the City's general plan; and (b) allow agricultural, grazing, open space and public uses within the district as interim uses; and

the proposed Reorganization Activities will maintain the status quo of land use designations, zoning, infrastructure, and municipal services, including the 2040 General Plan Update's "Future Study Area" designation and consistent SSZ pre-zoning. The SSZ pre-zoning is more restrictive than the County's current industrial zoning, reducing rather than increasing land use intensity; and do not propose any development or other physical change to the Hess-Laird Property or propose any particular action affecting the environment; and

on May 20, 2025, as the Lead Agency under the City Council of the City of American Canyon adopted Resolution No. 2025-37 certifying that the 2040 General Plan Update Final Program Environmental Impact Report ("General Plan EIR") (State Clearinghouse No. 2022070038) had been prepared in full compliance with CEQA and includes the Affected Territory at a program level of analysis, required mitigation measures, and a Mitigation Monitoring and Reporting Program (MMRP); and
for purposes of CEQA analysis the proposed Reorganization Activities and Pre-zoning are a project (Project); and
the proposed Project has been reviewed for consistency with the applicable General Plan, zoning, and other applicable land use regulations; and

Public Resources Code section 21083.3 and CEQA Guidelines section 15183 provide that projects which are consistent with the development density established by an existing General Plan, community plan, or zoning for which an EIR has been certified require no additional environmental review except as necessary to examine project-specific effects that are peculiar to the project or its site; and

in connection with the proposed Project, an Addendum to the 2040 General Plan Update Final Program Environmental Impact Report ("Addendum"), a copy of which is on file in the Community Development Department and attached as Exhibit C, has been prepared pursuant to Public Resources Code section 21166 and sections 15163-15164.7 of the State CEQA Guidelines (California Code of Regulations, Title 14, Division 6, Chapter 3) to determine whether any new or substantially more severe significant environmental impacts would result from the proposed reorganization; and
the City has reviewed and considered the Addendum together with the General Plan EIR and the entire administrative record; and

the proposed Affected Territory Pre-Zoning is a contemplated "Project Approval" under the General Plan EIR and the City is lead agency for reorganization actions pursuant to CEQA Guidelines section 15367; and
the Affected Territory is located in Napa Airport Land Use Compatibility Plan District Zones D1 and D2; and

allowable uses in the Special Study Pre-Zoning district, such as agricultural, grazing, open space and public uses are deemed "normally compatible" within the Napa Airport Land Use Compatibility Plan District Zones D1 and D2 (Exhibit 5-2); and
on July 30, 2026, the Planning Commission of the City of American Canyon conducted a public hearing and unanimously recommended City Council approval of the ordinance; and

a duly noticed public hearing was held by the City Council of the City of American Canyon on September 1, 2026, at which time all interested persons were given an opportunity to be heard regarding the proposed Municipal Code amendments.

BE IT ORDAINED that the City Council of the City of American Canyon hereby adopts the Affected Territory Pre-Zoning to Special Study Zone as described in American Canyon Municipal Code Chapter 19.50 based on the findings and depicted on Exhibit A and Exhibit B and attached hereto.

section.text: FINDINGS. The City Council finds based on the following evidence and as required by State Law on General Plan Amendments:

para.text: The proposed amendment is deemed to be in the public interest.

text.em: Pre-Zoning Special Study will achieve the project objectives listed in the Resolution recitals which include facilitating an orderly and public discussion, supported by technical analysis that will determine beneficial land uses in this area consistent with objectives in the American Canyon General Plan. Furthermore, permitting interim use of agriculture and open space uses demonstrates that the annexation is part of a longer-term, staged plan that avoids rushing the Affected Territories into development by maintaining agricultural resources until no longer needed.

para.text: The amendment is consistent with the purposes of this title, as set forth in Chapter 19.01, Authority, Purposes and Effects of the Zoning Ordinance.

text.em: The Pre-Zoning is consistent with the purpose of the Zoning Ordinance to protect and promote the public health, safety, peace, comfort, convenience, aesthetics, prosperity, and general welfare because the proposed Pre-Zoning regulations will maintain a low intensity of use prior to an orderly and transparent decision making process on optimal long-term land use or land uses in the Affected Territory.

section.text: CEQA FINDINGS: The Affected Territory Special Study General Plan designation was evaluated in the General Plan Program Environmental Impact Report (General Plan EIR) (SCH# 2022070038). Implementing Special Study Pre-Zoning and Reorganization Activities is a contemplated later "Project Approval" under the General Plan EIR.

para.text: The Project is consistent with the land use designation, development density, applicable General Plan policies, and zoning applicable to the Project site.

The City previously certified the General Plan EIR, which analyzed the environmental impacts associated with development contemplated by the General Plan, including development of the type and intensity proposed by the Project.
The City finds that the Project will not result in significant environmental effects that are peculiar to the Project which were not analyzed in the certified General Plan EIR.
The Project will not result in significant off-site or cumulative impacts that were not adequately analyzed in the certified General Plan EIR.

There is no substantial new information that was not known at the time the General Plan EIR was certified demonstrating that the Project would result in previously identified significant impacts that would be substantially more severe than disclosed in the prior EIR.

All applicable mitigation measures adopted in connection with certification of the General Plan EIR that are relevant to the Project have been incorporated into the Project or otherwise will be implemented through existing City ordinances, development standards, permit conditions, or other uniformly applied policies.
To the extent applicable, uniformly applied development policies, regulations, and standards adopted by the City substantially mitigate environmental effects associated with the Project.

Accordingly, pursuant to Public Resources Code section 21083.3 and CEQA Guidelines section 15183, no additional Environmental Impact Report, Mitigated Negative Declaration, or Negative Declaration is required because the Project is consistent with the development density established by the applicable General Plan and the certified General Plan EIR adequately addresses the environmental effects of the Project, subject only to implementation of applicable mitigation measures and uniformly applied development standards.
The Addendum to the General Plan EIR was prepared for Project in compliance with the requirements of CEQA and the CEQA Guidelines.

Based on the evidence submitted and as demonstrated by the analysis in the Addendum, and in light of the record as a whole, none of the conditions described in Public Resources Code section 21166 or CEQA Guidelines sections 15162 or 15163 calling for preparation of a subsequent or supplemental EIR or negative declaration have occurred. Specifically:

No substantial changes are proposed by the Project that will require major revisions of the General EIR due to the involvement of new significant environmental effects or a substantial increase in the severity of previously identified significant effects;

No substantial changes have occurred with respect to the circumstances under which these actions are undertaken that will require major revisions of the General Plan EIR due to the involvement of new significant environmental effects or a substantial increase in the severity of previously identified significant effects; or

No new information of substantial importance, which was not known and could not have been known with the exercise of reasonable diligence at the time the General Plan EIR was certified as complete and the 2040 General Plan Update was adopted, shows any of the following:
The Project will have one or more significant effects not discussed in the General Plan EIR;
Significant effects previously examined will be substantially more severe than shown in the General Plan EIR;

Mitigation measures or alternatives previously found not to be feasible would in fact be feasible and would substantially reduce one or more significant effects of the pre-zoning or Reorganization Activities, but the proponents decline to adopt the mitigation measure or alternative; or

Mitigation measures or alternatives that are considerably different from those analyzed in the General Plan EIR would substantially reduce one or more significant effects on the environment, but the proponents decline to adopt the mitigation measure or alternative.

The City has considered the Addendum in connection with the previously approved General Plan EIR and hereby finds on the basis of the whole record before it that based on substantial evidence the Project will have no significant effect on the environment. The Project not authorize development beyond the land uses, densities, intensities, and development assumptions analyzed in the General Plan EIR. The City further finds that the Addendum fully discloses and analyzes the environmental effects of the Project and reflects the City's independent judgment and analysis.

Pursuant to the above findings, the City Council of the City of American Canyon determines that the 2040 General Plan Update Final General Plan EIR and MMRP, together with the Addendum (Exhibit C), satisfy all requirements of CEQA and are adequate to serve as the required environmental documentation for the proposed Pre-zoning the Affected Territory and Reorganization Activities and, therefore, hereby approves and adopts the Addendum to the 2040 General Plan Update Final General Plan EIR.

The City Council hereby directs the Community Development Director or designee, to file a Notice of Determination in accordance with the requirements of the CEQA Guidelines and the Public Resources Code in accordance with Public Resources Code section 21152 and CEQA Guidelines sections 15075 and 15094, as applicable.

section.text: Napa Airport Land Use Compatibility Plan. The Pre-Zoning that accommodates agricultural, grazing, open space and public uses are considered "normally compatible" within Zones D1 and D2 of the Napa Airport Land Use Compatibility Plan (NALUCP) (Exhibit 5-2). Furthermore, the Pre-Zoning does not involve the types of airport impact concerns listed in Policy 2.3.1(a) which include:

para.text: Noise: Locations exposed to potentially disruptive levels of aircraft noise.

text.em: The proposed uses are deemed "normally compatible" within Zones D1 and D2.

para.text: Safety: Areas where the risk of an aircraft accident poses heightened safety concerns for people and property on the ground.

text.em: Zones D1 and D2 present minimal aircraft accident hazards coupled with extremely low population densities permitted within the proposed Pre-Zoning.

para.text: Airspace Protection: Places where height and various other land use characteristics need to be restricted in order to prevent creation of physical, visual, or electronic hazards to flight within the airspace required for operation of aircraft to and from the Airport.

text.em: The Affected Territory subject to the Pre-Zoning is approximately 1 mile at its closest point to the Napa Airport runway. The proposed agricultural, grazing, open space and public uses represent historical uses on the property and do not present a height characteristic that would impair physical, visual, or electronic hazards to flight within the airspace required for operation of aircraft to and from the Airport.

para.text: Overflight: Locations where aircraft overflying can be intrusive and annoying to many people.

text.em: The proposed uses are very low in population density and deemed "normally compatible" within Zones D1 and D2.

section.text: For reasons explained above, it can be concluded with certainty that the Affected Territory Pre-Zoning would not affect Napa County airport operations and therefore referral to the Napa County Airport Land Use Commission is not required.

Furthermore, the applicant received a voluntary project referral finding of consistency with the NALUCP consistent with NALUCP Section 2.6.1(c), by the ALUC Executive Director. A copy of the consistency determination is included as Exhibit D to this Ordinance.
EFFECTIVE DATE. This ordinance shall become effective effect 30 days after its final passage pursuant to Government Code section 36937.

SEVERABILITY. If any section, sentence, clause or phrase of this Ordinance is for any reason held to be invalid or unconstitutional by a decision of any court of competent jurisdiction, such decision shall not affect the validity of the remaining portions of this Ordinance. The City Council hereby declares that it would have passed this Ordinance and adopted this Ordinance and each section, sentence, clause or phrase thereof, irrespective of the fact that one or more sections, subsections, sentences, clauses or phrases be declared invalid or unconstitutional.

CUSTODIAN OF RECORDS. The documents and materials that constitute the record of proceedings on which this Ordinance is based are located at the City Clerk's office located at 4831 Broadway, Suite 201, American Canyon, CA 94503. The custodian of these records is the City Clerk.
